subject: Mythology
title: Perseus and the Head of Medusa
description: A quick, practical guide to Perseus and the Head of Medusa.

hook.text: Perseus was sent to kill Medusa, a monster whose gaze turned anyone who looked at her into stone.

buildup.text: The gods gave him tools: winged sandals from Hermes, a mirrored shield from Athena, and a magic bag.

discovery.text: He used the mirrored shield to see Medusa's reflection, then struck off her head without looking directly.

twist.text: From Medusa's neck sprang the winged horse Pegasus, born from her blood the moment she died.

climax.text: Perseus used her severed head as a weapon, turning his enemies to stone before returning it to Athena.

punchline.text: He defeated the monster by never looking at her.

quiz.question: How did Perseus avoid being turned to stone by Medusa?
options: He closed his eyes and struck blindly
He used a mirrored shield to see her reflection
He wore enchanted armor that blocked her gaze
